prompt: A food-delivery app's contribution per order fell from $3.10 to $2.40. The candidate's framework: (1) Average order value and commission rate; (2) Courier pay per order; (3) Payment and refund costs per order; (4) Number of orders per month. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 3 overlap: refunds lower the order value
options.feedback: Refunds are a cost the app bears after the sale; order value and commission are what it charges. They are separate lines.

options.text: Missing: what couriers earn for each delivery
options.feedback: Courier earnings per delivery are bucket 2.

options.text: It's a generic unit-economics list that would fit any delivery business
options.feedback: Unit economics per order is the right lens for a per-order margin. The flaw is bucket 4.

options.text: Bucket 4 doesn't belong: order volume doesn't change contribution per order
options.feedback: Right. Contribution per order is revenue minus variable costs on each order, so how many orders there are doesn't move it. Replace it with promotions and discounts per order.

explanation: Contribution per order = commission − courier pay − payment and refund costs − promotions. Volume changes total contribution, not contribution per order.

extras.corrected_framework: Order value and commission; courier pay; payment and refund costs; promotions per order
